passages.text: King Solomon, however, loved many foreign women along with the daughter of Pharaoh—women of Moab, Ammon, Edom, and Sidon, as well as Hittite women.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon was the ruler of Israel.
King Solomon loved many women.
These women were foreigners.
He also loved the daughter of Pharaoh from Egypt.
He loved women from Moab.
He loved women from Ammon.
He loved women from Edom.
He loved women from Sidon.
He loved Hittite women.
All these women were not Israelites.
King Solomon chose to love many foreign women.
passages.original: וְהַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה אָהַ֞ב נָשִׁ֧ים נָכְרִיּ֛וֹת רַבּ֖וֹת וְאֶת־ בַּת־ פַּרְעֹ֑ה מוֹאֲבִיּ֤וֹת עַמֳּנִיּוֹת֙ אֲדֹ֣מִיֹּ֔ת צֵדְנִיֹּ֖ת חִתִּיֹּֽת׃

passages.text: These women were from the nations about which the LORD had told the Israelites, “You must not intermarry with them, for surely they will turn your hearts after their gods.” Yet Solomon clung to these women in love.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to the Israelites.
He told them about certain nations.
He said, “You must not intermarry with these nations.”
He warned, “They will turn your hearts after their gods.”
These women came from those nations.
Solomon loved these women.
Solomon clung to them in love.
passages.original: מִן־ הַגּוֹיִ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָֽמַר־ יְהוָה֩ אֶל־ בְּנֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל לֹֽא־ תָבֹ֣אוּ בָהֶ֗ם וְהֵם֙ לֹא־ יָבֹ֣אוּ בָכֶ֔ם אָכֵן֙ יַטּ֣וּ אֶת־ לְבַבְכֶ֔ם אַחֲרֵ֖י אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֑ם בָּהֶ֛ם דָּבַ֥ק שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה לְאַהֲבָֽה׃

passages.text: He had seven hundred wives of royal birth and three hundred concubines—and his wives turned his heart away.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon was the ruler of Israel.
King Solomon had seven hundred wives.
All of these wives were of royal birth.
King Solomon also had three hundred concubines.
His wives turned his heart away.
passages.original: וַיְהִי־ ל֣וֹ נָשִׁ֗ים שָׂרוֹת֙ שְׁבַ֣ע מֵא֔וֹת וּפִֽלַגְשִׁ֖ים שְׁלֹ֣שׁ מֵא֑וֹת וַיַּטּ֥וּ נָשָׁ֖יו אֶת־ לִבּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: For when Solomon grew old, his wives turned his heart after other gods, and he was not wholeheartedly devoted to the LORD his God, as his father David had been.
passages.sermon:
Solomon was king of Israel.
Solomon grew old.
His wives turned his heart toward other gods.
Solomon did not remain fully devoted to the LORD his God.
David was Solomon’s father.
David had been fully devoted to the LORD.
Solomon was not like his father David.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י לְעֵת֙ זִקְנַ֣ת שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה נָשָׁיו֙ הִטּ֣וּ אֶת־ לְבָב֔וֹ אַחֲרֵ֖י אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֑ים וְלֹא־ הָיָ֨ה לְבָב֤וֹ שָׁלֵם֙ עִם־ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֔יו כִּלְבַ֖ב דָּוִ֥יד אָבִֽיו׃

passages.text: Solomon followed Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians and Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites.
passages.sermon:
Solomon was the king of Israel.
Solomon turned away from the LORD his God.
Solomon followed Ashtoreth.
Ashtoreth was the goddess of the Sidonians.
Solomon also followed Milcom.
Milcom was the abomination of the Ammonites.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה אַחֲרֵ֣י עַשְׁתֹּ֔רֶת אֱלֹהֵ֖י צִדֹנִ֑ים וְאַחֲרֵ֣י מִלְכֹּ֔ם שִׁקֻּ֖ץ עַמֹּנִֽים׃

passages.text: So Solomon did evil in the sight of the LORD; unlike his father David, he did not follow the LORD completely.
passages.sermon:
Solomon was the king of Israel.
Solomon did evil in the sight of the LORD.
Solomon did not follow the LORD completely.
David was Solomon’s father.
David had followed the LORD completely.
Solomon did not follow the LORD as David his father had done.
passages.original: וַיַּ֧עַשׂ שְׁלֹמֹ֛ה הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְלֹ֥א מִלֵּ֛א אַחֲרֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה כְּדָוִ֥ד אָבִֽיו׃ס

passages.text: At that time on a hill east of Jerusalem, Solomon built a high place for Chemosh the abomination of Moab and for Molech the abomination of the Ammonites.
passages.sermon:
Solomon was the king of Israel.
At that time, Solomon built a high place.
He built it on a hill east of Jerusalem.
He built the high place for Chemosh.
Chemosh was the abomination of Moab.
Solomon also built a high place for Molech.
Molech was the abomination of the Ammonites.
passages.original: אָז֩ יִבְנֶ֨ה שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה בָּמָ֗ה לִכְמוֹשׁ֙ שִׁקֻּ֣ץ מוֹאָ֔ב בָּהָ֕ר אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־ פְּנֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וּלְמֹ֕לֶךְ שִׁקֻּ֖ץ בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן׃

passages.text: He did the same for all his foreign wives, who burned incense and sacrificed to their gods.
passages.sermon:
Solomon was king of Israel.
He had many foreign wives.
These wives worshiped other gods.
Solomon built places of worship for them.
He did this for all his foreign wives.
These wives burned incense to their gods.
They offered sacrifices to their gods.
passages.original: וְכֵ֣ן עָשָׂ֔ה לְכָל־ נָשָׁ֖יו הַנָּכְרִיּ֑וֹת מַקְטִיר֥וֹת וּֽמְזַבְּח֖וֹת לֵאלֹהֵיהֶֽן׃

passages.text: Now the LORD grew angry with Solomon, because his heart had turned away from the LORD, the God of Israel, who had appeared to him twice.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD had appeared to Solomon two times.
Solomon was the king of Israel.
Solomon turned his heart away from the LORD.
The LORD became angry with Solomon.
passages.original: וַיִּתְאַנַּ֥ף יְהוָ֖ה בִּשְׁלֹמֹ֑ה כִּֽי־ נָטָ֣ה לְבָב֗וֹ מֵעִ֤ם יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הַנִּרְאָ֥ה אֵלָ֖יו פַּעֲמָֽיִם׃

passages.text: Although He had warned Solomon explicitly not to follow other gods, Solomon did not keep the LORD’s command.
passages.sermon:
God warned Solomon.
God told Solomon not to follow other gods.
God gave Solomon a clear command.
Solomon did not obey God’s command.
passages.original: וְצִוָּ֤ה אֵלָיו֙ עַל־ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה לְבִ֨לְתִּי־ לֶ֔כֶת אַחֲרֵ֖י אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֑ים וְלֹ֣א שָׁמַ֔ר אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־ צִוָּ֖ה יְהוָֽה׃פ

passages.text: Then the LORD said to Solomon, “Because you have done this and have not kept My covenant and My statutes, which I have commanded you, I will tear the kingdom away from you and give it to your servant.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Solomon.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD had appeared to Solomon twice.
The LORD said, “You have done this evil thing.
You did not keep My covenant.
You did not keep My statutes.
I commanded you to obey them.
Because of this, I will tear the kingdom away from you.
I will give the kingdom to your servant.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה לִשְׁלֹמֹ֗ה יַ֚עַן אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָֽיְתָה־ זֹּ֣את עִמָּ֔ךְ וְלֹ֤א שָׁמַ֙רְתָּ֙ בְּרִיתִ֣י וְחֻקֹּתַ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּ֖יתִי עָלֶ֑יךָ קָרֹ֨עַ אֶקְרַ֤ע אֶת־ הַמַּמְלָכָה֙ מֵֽעָלֶ֔יךָ וּנְתַתִּ֖יהָ לְעַבְדֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: Nevertheless, for the sake of your father David, I will not do it during your lifetime; I will tear it out of the hand of your son.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Solomon.
God said He would not take the kingdom from Solomon during Solomon’s life.
God said He would do this because of David, Solomon’s father.
God said He would take the kingdom from Solomon’s son instead.
passages.original: אַךְ־ בְּיָמֶ֙יךָ֙ לֹ֣א אֶעֱשֶׂ֔נָּה לְמַ֖עַן דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֑יךָ מִיַּ֥ד בִּנְךָ֖ אֶקְרָעֶֽנָּה׃

passages.text: Yet I will not tear the whole kingdom away from him. I will give one tribe to your son for the sake of My servant David and for the sake of Jerusalem, which I have chosen.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Solomon.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD said He would not take away the entire kingdom from Solomon’s son.
The LORD said He would leave one tribe for Solomon’s son.
The LORD would do this because of David, His servant.
The LORD would also do this because of Jerusalem.
The LORD had chosen Jerusalem.
passages.original: רַ֤ק אֶת־ כָּל־ הַמַּמְלָכָה֙ לֹ֣א אֶקְרָ֔ע שֵׁ֥בֶט אֶחָ֖ד אֶתֵּ֣ן לִבְנֶ֑ךָ לְמַ֙עַן֙ דָּוִ֣ד עַבְדִּ֔י וּלְמַ֥עַן יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּחָֽרְתִּי׃

passages.text: Then the LORD raised up against Solomon an adversary, Hadad the Edomite, from the royal line of Edom.
passages.sermon:
The LORD acted against Solomon.
The LORD raised up an adversary for Solomon.
This adversary was Hadad.
Hadad was an Edomite.
Hadad came from the royal family of Edom.
passages.original: וַיָּ֨קֶם יְהוָ֤ה שָׂטָן֙ לִשְׁלֹמֹ֔ה אֵ֖ת הֲדַ֣ד הָאֲדֹמִ֑י מִזֶּ֧רַע הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ ה֖וּא בֶּאֱדֽוֹם׃

passages.text: Earlier, when David was in Edom, Joab the commander of the army had gone to bury the dead and had struck down every male in Edom.
passages.sermon:
David was in Edom.
Joab was the commander of David’s army.
Joab went to Edom to bury the dead.
Joab struck down every male in Edom.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י בִּֽהְי֤וֹת דָּוִד֙ אֶת־ אֱד֔וֹם בַּעֲל֗וֹת יוֹאָב֙ שַׂ֣ר הַצָּבָ֔א לְקַבֵּ֖ר אֶת־ הַחֲלָלִ֑ים וַיַּ֥ךְ כָּל־ זָכָ֖ר בֶּאֱדֽוֹם׃

passages.text: Joab and all Israel had stayed there six months, until he had killed every male in Edom.
passages.sermon:
Joab was the commander of Israel’s army.
Joab and all Israel stayed in Edom for six months.
They remained there for this entire time.
Joab killed every male in Edom during these six months.
passages.original: כִּ֣י שֵׁ֧שֶׁת חֳדָשִׁ֛ים יָֽשַׁב־ שָׁ֥ם יוֹאָ֖ב וְכָל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל עַד־ הִכְרִ֥ית כָּל־ זָכָ֖ר בֶּאֱדֽוֹם׃

passages.text: But Hadad, still just a young boy, had fled to Egypt, along with some Edomites who were servants of his father.
passages.sermon:
Hadad was a young boy from Edom.
Joab, the commander of David’s army, had killed every male in Edom.
Hadad fled from Edom to Egypt.
Some Edomites went with him.
These men were servants of Hadad’s father.
passages.original: וַיִּבְרַ֣ח אֲדַ֡ד הוּא֩ וַאֲנָשִׁ֨ים אֲדֹמִיִּ֜ים מֵעַבְדֵ֥י אָבִ֛יו אִתּ֖וֹ לָב֣וֹא מִצְרָ֑יִם וַהֲדַ֖ד נַ֥עַר קָטָֽן׃

passages.text: Hadad and his men set out from Midian and went to Paran. They took men from Paran with them and went to Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt, who gave Hadad a house and land and provided him with food.
passages.sermon:
Hadad was a young Edomite boy.
Some Edomite servants of his father were with him.
Hadad and these men left Midian.
They traveled to Paran.
They took more men from Paran with them.
They all went to Egypt.
They came to Pharaoh, the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh gave Hadad a house.
Pharaoh gave Hadad food.
Pharaoh gave Hadad land.
passages.original: וַיָּקֻ֙מוּ֙ מִמִּדְיָ֔ן וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ פָּארָ֑ן וַיִּקְחוּ֩ אֲנָשִׁ֨ים עִמָּ֜ם מִפָּארָ֗ן וַיָּבֹ֤אוּ מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ אֶל־ פַּרְעֹ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ־ מִצְרַ֔יִם וַיִּתֶּן־ ל֣וֹ בַ֗יִת וְלֶ֙חֶם֙ אָ֣מַר ל֔וֹ וְאֶ֖רֶץ נָ֥תַן לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: There Hadad found such great favor in the sight of Pharaoh that he gave to him in marriage the sister of Queen Tahpenes, his own wife.
passages.sermon:
Hadad was a young Edomite boy.
He fled to Egypt with some of his father’s servants.
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh saw Hadad.
Pharaoh liked Hadad very much.
Pharaoh showed Hadad great favor.
Pharaoh gave Hadad a wife.
Pharaoh gave Hadad the sister of his own wife.
Pharaoh’s wife was Queen Tahpenes.
Hadad married the sister of Queen Tahpenes.
passages.original: וַיִּמְצָא֙ הֲדַ֥ד חֵ֛ן בְּעֵינֵ֥י פַרְעֹ֖ה מְאֹ֑ד וַיִּתֶּן־ ל֤וֹ אִשָּׁה֙ אֶת־ אֲח֣וֹת אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ אֲח֖וֹת תַּחְפְּנֵ֥יס הַגְּבִירָֽה׃

passages.text: And the sister of Tahpenes bore Hadad a son named Genubath. Tahpenes herself weaned him in Pharaoh’s palace, and Genubath lived there among the sons of Pharaoh.
passages.sermon:
Hadad was a man from Edom.
The sister of Tahpenes became Hadad’s wife.
She gave birth to a son for Hadad.
They named the son Genubath.
Tahpenes was the queen of Egypt.
Tahpenes herself weaned Genubath.
She did this inside Pharaoh’s palace.
Genubath lived in Pharaoh’s palace.
He grew up among the sons of Pharaoh.
passages.original: וַתֵּ֨לֶד ל֜וֹ אֲח֣וֹת תַּחְפְּנֵ֗יס אֵ֚ת גְּנֻבַ֣ת בְּנ֔וֹ וַתִּגְמְלֵ֣הוּ תַחְפְּנֵ֔ס בְּת֖וֹךְ בֵּ֣ית פַּרְעֹ֑ה וַיְהִ֤י גְנֻבַת֙ בֵּ֣ית פַּרְעֹ֔ה בְּת֖וֹךְ בְּנֵ֥י פַרְעֹֽה׃

passages.text: When Hadad heard in Egypt that David had rested with his fathers and that Joab, the commander of the army, was dead, he said to Pharaoh, “Let me go, that I may return to my own country.”
passages.sermon:
Hadad was living in Egypt.
David was the king of Israel.
Joab was the commander of David’s army.
David died and joined his ancestors.
Joab also died.
Hadad heard this news while he was in Egypt.
Hadad spoke to Pharaoh, the king of Egypt.
Hadad said, “Let me go.”
Hadad wanted to return to his own country.
passages.original: וַהֲדַ֞ד שָׁמַ֣ע בְּמִצְרַ֗יִם כִּֽי־ שָׁכַ֤ב דָּוִד֙ עִם־ אֲבֹתָ֔יו וְכִי־ מֵ֖ת יוֹאָ֣ב שַֽׂר־ הַצָּבָ֑א וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הֲדַד֙ אֶל־ פַּרְעֹ֔ה שַׁלְּחֵ֖נִי וְאֵלֵ֥ךְ אֶל־ אַרְצִֽי׃

passages.text: But Pharaoh asked him, “What have you lacked here with me that you suddenly want to go back to your own country?” “Nothing,” Hadad replied, “but please let me go.”
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Hadad was living in Egypt with Pharaoh.
Pharaoh spoke to Hadad.
Pharaoh asked Hadad a question.
Pharaoh said, “What have you lacked while you were with me?”
Pharaoh said, “Why do you want to go back to your own country?”
Hadad answered Pharaoh.
Hadad said, “I have not lacked anything.”
Hadad said, “But please let me go.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר ל֣וֹ פַרְעֹ֗ה כִּ֠י מָה־ אַתָּ֤ה חָסֵר֙ עִמִּ֔י וְהִנְּךָ֥ מְבַקֵּ֖שׁ לָלֶ֣כֶת אֶל־ אַרְצֶ֑ךָ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר׀ לֹ֔א כִּ֥י שַׁלֵּ֖חַ תְּשַׁלְּחֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: And God raised up against Solomon another adversary, Rezon the son of Eliada, who had fled from his master, Hadadezer king of Zobah, and had gathered men to himself. When David killed the Zobaites, Rezon captained a band of raiders and went to Damascus, where they settled and gained control.
passages.sermon:
God acted against Solomon.
God raised up an adversary for Solomon.
This adversary was Rezon.
Rezon was the son of Eliada.
Rezon had fled from his master.
His master was Hadadezer.
Hadadezer was king of Zobah.
Rezon gathered men to himself.
David killed the people of Zobah.
After this, Rezon became the leader of a band of raiders.
Rezon and his men went to Damascus.
They settled in Damascus.
Rezon and his men ruled in Damascus.
passages.original: וַיָּ֨קֶם אֱלֹהִ֥ים לוֹ֙ שָׂטָ֔ן אֶת־ רְז֖וֹן בֶּן־ אֶלְיָדָ֑ע אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּרַ֗ח מֵאֵ֛ת הֲדַדְעֶ֥זֶר מֶֽלֶךְ־ צוֹבָ֖ה אֲדֹנָֽיו׃ וַיִּקְבֹּ֤ץ עָלָיו֙ אֲנָשִׁ֔ים וַיְהִ֣י שַׂר־ גְּד֔וּד בַּהֲרֹ֥ג דָּוִ֖ד אֹתָ֑ם וַיֵּלְכ֤וּ דַמֶּ֙שֶׂק֙ וַיֵּ֣שְׁבוּ בָ֔הּ וַֽיִּמְלְכ֖וּ בְּדַמָּֽשֶׂק׃

passages.text: Rezon was Israel’s enemy throughout the days of Solomon, adding to the trouble caused by Hadad. So Rezon ruled over Aram with hostility toward Israel.
passages.sermon:
Rezon was an enemy of Israel.
He opposed Israel during all the days of King Solomon.
Hadad also caused trouble for Israel.
Rezon added to this trouble.
Rezon ruled over Aram.
He ruled with hostility toward Israel.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֨י שָׂטָ֤ן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל֙ כָּל־ יְמֵ֣י שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה וְאֶת־ הָרָעָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֲדָ֑ד וַיָּ֙קָץ֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיִּמְלֹ֖ךְ עַל־ אֲרָֽם׃פ

passages.text: Now Jeroboam son of Nebat was an Ephraimite from Zeredah whose mother was a widow named Zeruah. Jeroboam was a servant of Solomon, but he rebelled against the king, and this is the account of his rebellion against the king. Solomon had built the supporting terraces and repaired the gap in the wall of the city of his father David.
passages.sermon:
Jeroboam was the son of Nebat.
Jeroboam was an Ephraimite.
He came from Zeredah.
His mother was Zeruah.
Zeruah was a widow.
Jeroboam served Solomon.
Jeroboam rebelled against King Solomon.
This is how Jeroboam rebelled against the king.
Solomon built the supporting terraces.
Solomon repaired the gap in the wall of the city of David, his father.
passages.original: וְיָרָבְעָם֩ בֶּן־ נְבָ֨ט אֶפְרָתִ֜י מִן־ הַצְּרֵדָ֗ה וְשֵׁ֤ם אִמּוֹ֙ צְרוּעָה֙ אִשָּׁ֣ה אַלְמָנָ֔ה עֶ֖בֶד לִשְׁלֹמֹ֑ה וַיָּ֥רֶם יָ֖ד בַּמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ וְזֶ֣ה הַדָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁר־ הֵרִ֥ים יָ֖ד בַּמֶּ֑לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה֙ בָּנָ֣ה אֶת־ הַמִּלּ֔וֹא סָגַ֕ר אֶת־ פֶּ֕רֶץ עִ֖יר דָּוִ֥ד אָבִֽיו׃

passages.text: Now Jeroboam was a mighty man of valor. So when Solomon noticed that the young man was industrious, he put him in charge of the whole labor force of the house of Joseph.
passages.sermon:
Jeroboam was a mighty man of valor.
He was strong and brave.
Solomon was the king of Israel.
Solomon saw that Jeroboam was a young man who worked hard.
Jeroboam was industrious.
Solomon put Jeroboam in charge of the entire labor force of the house of Joseph.
Jeroboam became the leader over all the workers from the tribe of Joseph.
passages.original: וְהָאִ֥ישׁ יָרָבְעָ֖ם גִּבּ֣וֹר חָ֑יִל וַיַּ֨רְא שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה אֶת־ הַנַּ֗עַר כִּֽי־ עֹשֵׂ֤ה מְלָאכָה֙ ה֔וּא וַיַּפְקֵ֣ד אֹת֔וֹ לְכָל־ סֵ֖בֶל בֵּ֥ית יוֹסֵֽף׃ס

passages.text: During that time, the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite met Jeroboam on the road as he was going out of Jerusalem. Now Ahijah had wrapped himself in a new cloak, and the two of them were alone in the open field.
passages.sermon:
Jeroboam was leaving Jerusalem.
Ahijah was a prophet from Shiloh.
Ahijah met Jeroboam on the road.
Ahijah had covered himself with a new cloak.
Only Ahijah and Jeroboam were in the field.
No one else was with them.
passages.original: וַֽיְהִי֙ בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔יא וְיָֽרָבְעָ֖ם יָצָ֣א מִירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וַיִּמְצָ֣א אֹת֡וֹ אֲחִיָּה֩ הַשִּׁילֹנִ֨י הַנָּבִ֜יא בַּדֶּ֗רֶךְ וְה֤וּא מִתְכַּסֶּה֙ בְּשַׂלְמָ֣ה חֲדָשָׁ֔ה וּשְׁנֵיהֶ֥ם לְבַדָּ֖ם בַּשָּׂדֶֽה׃

passages.text: And Ahijah took hold of the new cloak he was wearing, tore it into twelve pieces, and said to Jeroboam, “Take ten pieces for yourself, for this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘Behold, I will tear the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and I will give you ten tribes.
passages.sermon:
Ahijah was a prophet.
Ahijah wore a new cloak.
Ahijah took hold of his new cloak.
Ahijah tore the cloak into twelve pieces.
Ahijah spoke to Jeroboam.
Ahijah told Jeroboam, "Take ten pieces for yourself."
Ahijah said, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says."
The LORD says, "I will tear the kingdom out of Solomon’s hand."
The LORD says, "I will give you ten tribes."
passages.original: וַיִּתְפֹּ֣שׂ אֲחִיָּ֔ה בַּשַּׂלְמָ֥ה הַחֲדָשָׁ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָלָ֑יו וַיִּ֨קְרָעֶ֔הָ שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָׂ֖ר קְרָעִֽים׃ וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ לְיָֽרָבְעָ֔ם קַח־ לְךָ֖ עֲשָׂרָ֣ה קְרָעִ֑ים כִּ֣י כֹה֩ אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הִנְנִ֨י קֹרֵ֤עַ אֶת־ הַמַּמְלָכָה֙ מִיַּ֣ד שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה וְנָתַתִּ֣י לְךָ֔ אֵ֖ת עֲשָׂרָ֥ה הַשְּׁבָטִֽים׃

passages.text: But one tribe will remain for the sake of My servant David and for the sake of Jerusalem, the city I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel.
passages.sermon:
God spoke about the kingdom of Israel.
God said He would give most of the tribes to Jeroboam.
But God would let one tribe remain with Solomon’s family.
God did this for the sake of His servant David.
God also did this for the sake of Jerusalem.
God chose Jerusalem from all the tribes of Israel.
God chose Jerusalem to be His special city.
passages.original: וְהַשֵּׁ֥בֶט הָאֶחָ֖ד יִֽהְיֶה־ לּ֑וֹ לְמַ֣עַן׀ עַבְדִּ֣י דָוִ֗ד וּלְמַ֙עַן֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם הָעִיר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּחַ֣רְתִּי בָ֔הּ מִכֹּ֖ל שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: For they have forsaken Me to worship Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, Chemosh the god of the Moabites, and Milcom the god of the Ammonites. They have not walked in My ways, nor done what is right in My eyes, nor kept My statutes and judgments, as Solomon’s father David did.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel turned away from God.
They abandoned the LORD, the God of Israel.
They worshiped other gods.
They bowed down to Ashtoreth, the goddess of the Sidonians.
They served Chemosh, the god of the Moabites.
They honored Milcom, the god of the Ammonites.
They did not follow God's ways.
They did not do what is right in God's eyes.
They did not keep God's statutes.
They did not obey God's judgments.
David, Solomon’s father, did obey God.
David did what was right in God’s eyes.
David kept God’s statutes and judgments.
passages.original: יַ֣עַן׀ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עֲזָב֗וּנִי וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲווּ֮ לְעַשְׁתֹּרֶת֮ אֱלֹהֵ֣י צִֽדֹנִין֒ לִכְמוֹשׁ֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י מוֹאָ֔ב וּלְמִלְכֹּ֖ם אֱלֹהֵ֣י בְנֵֽי־ עַמּ֑וֹן וְלֹֽא־ הָלְכ֣וּ בִדְרָכַ֗י לַעֲשׂ֨וֹת הַיָּשָׁ֧ר בְּעֵינַ֛י וְחֻקֹּתַ֥י וּמִשְׁפָּטַ֖י כְּדָוִ֥ד אָבִֽיו׃

passages.text: Nevertheless, I will not take the whole kingdom out of Solomon’s hand, because I have made him ruler all the days of his life for the sake of David My servant, whom I chose because he kept My commandments and statutes.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about Solomon, the king of Israel.
God says, “I will not take the whole kingdom from Solomon’s hand.
I will let Solomon remain ruler all the days of his life.
I do this for the sake of My servant David.
I chose David because he kept My commandments and statutes.”
passages.original: וְלֹֽא־ אֶקַּ֥ח אֶת־ כָּל־ הַמַּמְלָכָ֖ה מִיָּד֑וֹ כִּ֣י׀ נָשִׂ֣יא אֲשִׁתֶ֗נּוּ כֹּ֚ל יְמֵ֣י חַיָּ֔יו לְמַ֨עַן דָּוִ֤ד עַבְדִּי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּחַ֣רְתִּי אֹת֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁמַ֖ר מִצְוֺתַ֥י וְחֻקֹּתָֽי׃

passages.text: But I will take ten tribes of the kingdom from the hand of his son and give them to you.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about the kingdom of Israel.
God says He will act.
God will take the kingdom from Solomon’s son.
God will take ten tribes from Solomon’s son.
God will give these ten tribes to you.
passages.original: וְלָקַחְתִּ֥י הַמְּלוּכָ֖ה מִיַּ֣ד בְּנ֑וֹ וּנְתַתִּ֣יהָ לְּךָ֔ אֵ֖ת עֲשֶׂ֥רֶת הַשְּׁבָטִֽים׃

passages.text: I will give one tribe to his son, so that My servant David will always have a lamp before Me in Jerusalem, the city where I chose to put My Name.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about Solomon’s son.
God says, “I will give one tribe to Solomon’s son.
I do this for the sake of My servant David.
David is My chosen servant.
David obeyed My commandments and statutes.
I want David to always have a lamp before Me.
This means David’s family will always have a descendant before Me.
This will happen in Jerusalem.
Jerusalem is the city I chose for Myself.
I chose Jerusalem to put My Name there.”
passages.original: וְלִבְנ֖וֹ אֶתֵּ֣ן שֵֽׁבֶט־ אֶחָ֑ד לְמַ֣עַן הֱיֽוֹת־ נִ֣יר לְדָֽוִיד־ עַ֠בְדִּי כָּֽל־ הַיָּמִ֤ים׀ לְפָנַי֙ בִּיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם הָעִיר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּחַ֣רְתִּי לִ֔י לָשׂ֥וּם שְׁמִ֖י שָֽׁם׃

passages.text: But as for you, I will take you, and you shall reign over all that your heart desires, and you will be king over Israel.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Jeroboam.
God said, “I will take you.
You will rule over everything your heart desires.
You will be king over Israel.”
passages.original: וְאֹתְךָ֣ אֶקַּ֔ח וּמָ֣לַכְתָּ֔ בְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־ תְּאַוֶּ֖ה נַפְשֶׁ֑ךָ וְהָיִ֥יתָ מֶּ֖לֶךְ עַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: If you listen to all that I command you, walk in My ways, and do what is right in My sight in order to keep My statutes and commandments as My servant David did, then I will be with you. I will build you a lasting dynasty just as I built for David, and I will give Israel to you.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Jeroboam.
God gave Jeroboam a command.
God said, “If you listen to everything I command you,
and if you walk in My ways,
and if you do what is right in My eyes,
and if you keep My statutes and My commandments,
as My servant David did,
then I will be with you.
I will build a faithful house for you.
This house will last, just as I built for David.
I will give you Israel.”
passages.original: וְהָיָ֗ה אִם־ תִּשְׁמַע֮ אֶת־ כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֲצַוֶּךָ֒ וְהָלַכְתָּ֣ בִדְרָכַ֗י וְעָשִׂ֨יתָ הַיָּשָׁ֤ר בְּעֵינַי֙ לִשְׁמ֤וֹר חֻקּוֹתַי֙ וּמִצְוֺתַ֔י כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה דָּוִ֣ד עַבְדִּ֑י וְהָיִ֣יתִי עִמָּ֗ךְ וּבָנִ֨יתִי לְךָ֤ בַֽיִת־ נֶאֱמָן֙ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּנִ֣יתִי לְדָוִ֔ד וְנָתַתִּ֥י לְךָ֖ אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: Because of this, I will humble David’s descendants—but not forever.’ ”
passages.sermon:
God spoke about David’s descendants.
God said He would humble David’s descendants because of these events.
God said He would not humble them forever.
God’s humbling of David’s descendants would last only for a time.
passages.original: וַֽאעַנֶּ֛ה אֶת־ זֶ֥רַע דָּוִ֖ד לְמַ֣עַן זֹ֑את אַ֖ךְ לֹ֥א כָל־ הַיָּמִֽים׃ס

passages.text: Solomon therefore sought to kill Jeroboam. But Jeroboam arose and fled to Egypt, to Shishak king of Egypt, where he remained until the death of Solomon.
passages.sermon:
Solomon was king over all Israel.
Solomon wanted to kill Jeroboam.
Jeroboam learned about this.
Jeroboam got up and escaped.
Jeroboam fled to Egypt.
Shishak was the king of Egypt.
Jeroboam stayed in Egypt.
Jeroboam remained there until Solomon died.
passages.original: וַיְבַקֵּ֥שׁ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה לְהָמִ֣ית אֶת־ יָרָבְעָ֑ם וַיָּ֣קָם יָרָבְעָ֗ם וַיִּבְרַ֤ח מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ אֶל־ שִׁישַׁ֣ק מֶֽלֶךְ־ מִצְרַ֔יִם וַיְהִ֥י בְמִצְרַ֖יִם עַד־ מ֥וֹת שְׁלֹמֹֽה׃

passages.text: As for the rest of the acts of Solomon—all that he did, as well as his wisdom—are they not written in the Book of the Acts of Solomon?
passages.sermon:
Solomon was king of Israel.
Solomon ruled in Jerusalem.
Solomon did many things.
Solomon showed great wisdom.
People recorded Solomon’s other acts.
People wrote about Solomon’s wisdom.
They wrote these things in the Book of the Acts of Solomon.
passages.original: וְיֶ֨תֶר דִּבְרֵ֧י שְׁלֹמֹ֛ה וְכָל־ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה וְחָכְמָת֑וֹ הֲלֽוֹא־ הֵ֣ם כְּתֻבִ֔ים עַל־ סֵ֖פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י שְׁלֹמֹֽה׃

passages.text: Thus the time that Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel was forty years.
passages.sermon: Solomon was king in Jerusalem.\r\nHe ruled over all Israel.\r\nHe reigned for forty years.
passages.original: וְהַיָּמִ֗ים אֲשֶׁר֩ מָלַ֨ךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֤ה בִירוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ עַל־ כָּל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַרְבָּעִ֖ים שָׁנָֽה׃

passages.text: And Solomon rested with his fathers and was buried in the city of his father David. And his son Rehoboam reigned in his place.
passages.sermon:
Solomon was king of Israel.
Solomon died.
People buried Solomon in the city of David.
David was Solomon’s father.
Rehoboam was Solomon’s son.
Rehoboam became king after Solomon.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב שְׁלֹמֹה֙ עִם־ אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַיִּ֨קָּבֵ֔ר בְּעִ֖יר דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֑יו וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ רְחַבְעָ֥ם בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃ס
